experiment.name: phase1_polarity
description: Is the +15 mW A/A offset a harness bias tied to the condition index, or
is it part of the operand effect?
phase1_traffic_volume replicated the depth-axis result but failed its A/A
gate: with both selectors identical, cond 1 read high in all three repeats
(+18.6, +10.1, +17.5 mW; between-SD 4.6). The offset is in RAPL ticks, not
in the sampling interval, so it is real package energy. Drift, transition
cost and predecessor-condition were each ruled out, and the monitor loop
has no cond-dependent branch. Mechanism unidentified.
Every run so far has used selectors [0, HW32] in that order, so a genuine
operand effect E and a condition-index bias B are perfectly confounded --
both add to cond 1. Running the reverse mapping separates them:
forward  [0, HW32]   ->  d = +E + B
reverse  [HW32, 0]   ->  d = -E + B
so  (fwd - rev)/2 = E   and   (fwd + rev)/2 = B
B is estimated far better from the A/A runs than from that average: on a
victim with E ~ 2 W the between-run SD is 65 mW, so (fwd+rev)/2 over four
repeats has SE ~23 mW and cannot resolve 15 mW, while four repeats of an
A/A (between-SD 4.6 mW) give SE ~2 mW. The polarity pair is therefore the
test that E flips sign cleanly and that B sits on top additively; the A/A
pair is the measurement of B.
The A/As run on ws_l3_x8, not the ws_dram_x8 used in the sweep. Same B on
a different victim at a different baseline power means the bias belongs to
the measurement path, not to the victim. Two A/A flavours (all-zero and
all-ones operands) also test whether it depends on the operand value.
Driver settings are identical to phase1_traffic_volume so the effects are
directly comparable; the block-order seed differs, so the four repeats are
four shuffles distinct from that sweep's -- if B is an artifact of a
particular block order it cannot survive that.

runs.label: aa_l3_ones
runs.comment: B with an all-ones working set; matches the sweep's A/A operand.

runs.label: aa_l3_zero
runs.comment: B with an all-zero working set; B must not depend on the value.

runs.label: l3_forward
runs.comment: +E + B. Same mapping every run so far has used.

runs.label: l3_reverse
runs.comment: -E + B. A real operand effect flips; an index bias does not.
